notes: The declared-expected differences for compare_m1_m6.py. THIS FILE IS A WHITELIST. Every entry
suppresses a finding that F-17(b) would otherwise report, so widening it is a reviewable diff
and never an edit made at measurement time. compare_m1_m6.py refuses (exit 5) any entry whose
citation does not resolve, and -- since 2026-08-25 -- any multi-field entry that offers one
citation for the whole list rather than one citation per field.
THE ACCEPTED PATTERN GRAMMAR, TRANSCRIBED 2026-08-25 FROM GRADED BEHAVIOUR, NOT FROM INTENT.
The prior sentence here described the guard as refusing 'a bare measurement id or a pattern
that ends in a wildcard segment'. That was the SUPERSEDED deny-list and it UNDERSTATED the
guard: it was the description that let defect D-3 through, because 'M-1[*' neither is a bare
id nor ends in a wildcard segment. The guard was replaced at c8a29082 by a positive grammar
and independently graded at 69dafb2c. What follows is transcribed from section 8 of
GRADE-20260825-d3-comparator-repair-fitness.md, which enumerated it by RUNNING bad_pattern at
compare_m1_m6.py = 68b4af12 rather than by reading it. If the code and this note disagree, the
CODE governs and this note is the defect -- that is the direction the last one failed in.
ACCEPTED
M-k.<field>              k in {3,4,5,6}, <field> a literal containing no '*'
M-1[<literal path>].<f>  the per-file form with a literal file path
M-1[*].<field>           the bare per-file wildcard
M-1[<partial>*].<field>  a PARTIAL selector -- accepted, and see the open question below
REFUSED, with the reason the guard itself prints
*, behind, M-7.x         does not begin with a measurement id
M-4, M-1                 bare measurement id; name the fields
M-4behind                after the id the next character must be '.' or '['
M-1.present              M-1 is measured per file; it needs a selector
M-1[ , M-1[*             the '[' selector is never closed -- THIS SHAPE IS D-3
M-1[] , M-1[].x          the selector is empty
M-1[*]                   after ']' the next character must be '.'
M-4. , M-1[*].           the field name is empty
M-4.* , M-4.head* ,      ANY '*' in the terminal field name. The wildcard is a
M-3.*x , M-4.*e* ,       SELECTOR-space device: legal inside M-1[...] where it ranges
M-4.behin* , M-1[*].*    over files, and nowhere else.
M-6[* , M-3[x].y         only M-1 is measured per file
M-2.importable and any   the perishable claim is NEVER suppressible
other M-2 field
(backstop)               the guard and the matcher disagree about what the pattern
reaches -- fails closed
The empty string and non-strings are refused as 'a field pattern must be a non-empty string'.
OPEN QUESTION, ESCALATED TO JOSEPH AND NOT SETTLED HERE. The PARTIAL selector row above
(M-1[nd-*].present) was ruled by the independent grader to be case (c): an AMBIGUITY requiring
a specification decision, not a behaviour already admitted and not an enlargement. Measured, on
the real M1_FILES population and with no hypothetical:
M-1[nd-unfolding/unified_throw_cov*].first_insert is ACCEPTED with no warning and reaches TWO
files -- unified_throw_cov.py and unified_throw_cov_5d.py -- while the literal form reaches
one. The guard REFUSES M-4.behin*, which reaches one field today, on the stated ground that a
wildcard 'would whitelist more than one'. It applies that reasoning in field space and not in
selector space.
The grader's recommendation, which is a recommendation and not a ruling, is to narrow the
selector to '*'-or-literal; the measured cost of doing so today is zero, because no entry in
this file uses a partial selector. UNTIL JOSEPH RULES, do not add one: the grade's condition of
fitness is that the expected list in force at filing time contains no partial M-1 selector.
ONE ENTRY OVER ONE FIELD. M-4.ahead WAS in the entry below and was REMOVED on 2026-08-25 after
a peer read the citation instead of trusting it. The cited document mentions ahead exactly
once, as `ahead = 0 ; --is-ancestor rc=0` -- a stable zero, and affirmative evidence that the
tree carried no commits of its own -- while its heading and its drift paragraph are both about
the BEHIND-count. The citation recorded the opposite of the field it was licensing. Do not
re-add it without a citation that is ABOUT ahead: the field moves either because someone pushed
the measured tree's commits to the upstream (harmless) or because that tree GAINED a commit
nobody else has (the drift F-17 exists to surface), and a whitelist may not swallow the second
to spare a reviewer the first.
DELIBERATELY NOT PRESENT. The SPEC also offered 'M-1, M-5 and M-6 are falsified by any commit
to build-k0-execution-integrity'. That is REJECTED: measured 2026-08-25 at 49dbdf8f, only 10
of the 46 COMMITS in 8c156a37..build-k0-execution-integrity touch any file in those three
populations, so 36 of 46 cannot move them and 'any commit' is false. THE PER-POPULATION
FIGURES, WITH THE UNIT OF EACH, because the parenthetical that stood here mixed two units and
a grader caught it: M-1 = 2 COMMITS touching 7 of its 10 FILES; M-5 = 8 COMMITS touching 8 of
its 8 FILES (both 8, which is the coincidence that made the mixed reading look consistent);
M-6 = 3 COMMITS touching its 1 FILE. The earlier note read '2 of 10 M-1 files', which states a
COMMIT count in the grammar of a FILE count, in the one artifact a reviewer reads to decide
whether this rejection was sound. Worse, as an entry it would have suppressed the
actual F-17(a) findings -- M-1's dropped tenth entrypoint and M-5's 0-of-8 against 8-of-8.
That one had no citation offered at all, which is a DIFFERENT defect from the ahead one: it was
refuted by measurement, not by its own evidence.
NO doc_sha256 IS DECLARED below, and that is a choice: the cited document is classed LIVE/open,
so pinning its digest would turn a peer's correction into a refusal at measurement time, which
is precisely the moment at which nobody should be widening a whitelist. The instrument records
the measured digest of every cited document in its output regardless, and it does enforce a
declared doc_sha256 when one is present.
WHAT NO CHECK HERE CAN DO: resolving is not supporting. The guard proves a quote EXISTS in a
named document; only a reader can say whether it is ABOUT the field. That is the review this
file exists to make possible, and it is why every suppressed field now carries its own quote.

entries.why: M-4.behind is a left-right count against --upstream, which defaults to origin/main (measure_m1_m6.py, the --upstream argument). The cited block records it moving 36 -> 55 -> 65 while HEAD, dirty and the 717/4 split are all unchanged in that same block -- drift demonstrated with the measured tree held FIXED, which is what licenses the suppression. NOT M-4.ahead (removed 2026-08-25; the same citation records it as a stable zero, see the notes). NOT M-4.upstream: two invocations run against different upstreams are not the same comparison. NOT M-4.head or M-4.dirty: those are the tree's identity, and a difference in them is the finding F-17(b) asks for.
